context: A Saturday morning phone call. Six-year-old Sho calls his grandpa Goro in Fukuoka. He has news.
purpose: tiny grandkid-grandparent call — small joy delivered with no preamble

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.style: Slow gravelly opening, almost a double-beat. Kyushu drawl settling in. Warm but not effusive. The kind of hello that is actually listening.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: おじいちゃん、しょうです。
lines.style: Formal and small, each syllable careful. A child introducing himself with a quiet kind of pride. Almost formal, like he's learned how to do this right.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.style: A small smile audible in the voice. Warm recognition settling into genuine pleasure. Slow enough to let the moment breathe. Real affection, no performance.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 元気。今日ね、自転車、乗れた。
lines.en: I'm doing well. Today — I rode my bike.
lines.style: A small breathless delivery, the whole reason for calling rising in his chest. Building slightly on the second phrase. The news tumbling out once he starts.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.style: Genuine astonishment breaking through, even and especially because he was probably already expecting this. A beat of real surprise. Slow, warm.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Pure six-year-old certainty, voice bouncing with newly-earned confidence. A small laugh lives in the delivery. Bright attack on the first word, unburdening himself of doubt.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.jp: えらいなあ。今度、見せて。
lines.en: That's impressive. Show me next time.
lines.style: Slow, deliberate, genuinely proud. Each word carries weight — not effusive, but earned. The voice of a man recognizing something real. Quiet conviction underneath.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: うん！…おじいちゃん、ありがとう。
lines.style: The first word bright and immediate, then a sudden shift into something quieter. A small pause before he thanks him. The gratitude doesn't explain itself — just sits there, genuine and undefended.
